text.p: PhoneTel Technologies Inc and Communications Central Inc said Tuesday they were evaluating the impact that a court decision on their industry might have on their proposed merger.

The companies said in a joint statement that a federal appellate court had asked the Federal Communications Commission to provide more information about how it had calculated a "dial-around" compensation for pay phone providers.
The commission requires long-distance carriers to compensate pay phone operators like PhoneTel and Communications Central for the coinless calls that its customers make.
Calling cards and toll-free numbers allow coinless calls at pay phones.
"The parties are engaged in discussions concerning a possible restructuring of such transaction in light of the ruling," they said.
In May, PhoneTel said it had extended until August 5 its tender offer to buy all outstanding shares of Communications Central.
It said 95 percent of the shares had been tendered to it.
The company official said PhoneTel was still looking to complete its financing of the deal.
